question: The Spanish Civil Guard’s Central Operational Unit (UCO) has obtained a file from public company ADIF on a contract awarded to Levantina Ingeniería y Construcción SL (B97016125) as part of corruption investigations into the Sánchez Government (Koldo case). The file contains suspected payments linked to contracts awarded by the Directorate-General for Roads1.

Between 2021 and 2023, the company was awarded at least three contracts by the government worth EUR 4.4 million for works funded by the ERDF or under NextGenerationEU2. Given that former senior government officials are in prison for bribery, embezzlement and influence peddling in relation to public contracts: 1.
Will the Commission investigate whether alleged corrupt practices linked to former senior officials in the Sánchez government also involved EU-funded contracts, such as the Levantina contracts?
Will it require Spain to repay the EU funds disbursed for each contract, including the company’s share in joint ventures if wrongdoing is detected?
Following all the cases of corruption surrounding Pedro Sánchez, has the Commission launched specific audits to ensure that EU funds allocated by the Spanish Government have not been misappropriated?
